newsitem.title: USA: CSCE sugar called to open little changed.
newsitem.headline: CSCE sugar called to open little changed.

text.p: CSCE world sugar futures were called to open barely changed on Monday, dealers said.

The benchmark October contract is expected to run into resistance around current levels, with the immediate upside target pegged at the recent high of 10.87 cents followed by Friday's high of 11.93 cents.
Friday, brisk fund buying carried CSCE world sugar futures sharply up with all delivery months out to January 1999 hitting new contract highs.
October ended up 0.31 cent at 11.86 cents a pound, after seeing a new contract high at 11.93 cents, the highest level in nearby CSCE sugar since last October.
The October/March spread narrowed to 0.18 cent, up from a low of 0.28 cent on Monday.
In fundamental news, Syria's General Foreign Trade Organization for Chemicals and Foodstuffs (GEZA) issued a tender to buy 26,000 tonnes of white sugar and 26,000 tonnes of raws for October delivery.

The second German sugar beet test for 1997/98 showed a sugar yield of 6.24 tonnes per hectare compared with 6.07 tonnes in the second test of the previous season, the sugar industry association WVZ said.
The second Ukranian sugar beet test showed an average sugar content of 11.4 percent, down from last year's 12.5 percent, the Agro-Industrial Complex Ministry said.
Traders in Indonesia said the country could import between 1.0 million and 1.1 million tonnes of mixed sugar in 1997, nearly unchanged from last year.
In London, white sugar futures were mixed in thin trade Monday. At 0850 EDT/1250 GMT, LIFFE October was $1.10 lower at $327.50. The rest of the board stood 10 cents higher to 60 cents lower.
